theWrapper.maxRetriesRationale: 0 on purpose: a retry after a partial promote re-runs an already-partial promotion (boundary-edge atoms are persisted before the property atoms).
theWrapper.whyTheBakedArgsAreTheDryLeg: A bare `gcloud run jobs execute hauska-engine-depth-warm-remint` must not be able to fire a live in-place upsert of a real atom. Baking the dry leg makes the write require a deliberate --args override, which mirrors the P-169 atoms-writer job being left deliberately unspecialized ('no --writer is baked, so every execution names its own writer, county and target'). A bare execute with no --args at all also cannot write: --row-id is REQUIRED and the runner FATALs without it.

theDryLeg.whyItIsSafeByConstruction: it is the same emit that promote.ts makes (emitDepthWarmPromotion is pure and touches no store) and it never calls a write path; writePropertyAtomIfEnabled is not reached because promoteDepthWarmToStorage is only called when input.promote && input.storage.

theThreeStatesItDistinguishes.conflictPresent_true: the A-148 (stale-numeric-columns) or R-1 (second-source) detector fired; the body carries displayMeta.secondSource.conflict and the surfaces' one conflict sentence survives the re-mint. Proceed.
theThreeStatesItDistinguishes.noOpForConflict_true (secondSourcePresen: SUCCESSFUL NO-OP FOR THE REMIT'S PURPOSE. The detectors did not fire; the apply leg exits 0, increments its promoted/verifyPass counts, and changes nothing about the disclosure. The operator must not read exit 0 as 'the risk is now wired'.
theThreeStatesItDistinguishes.deletesExistingDisclosure_true (secondSo: REGRESSION, NOT A NO-OP. The emitted body carries no secondSource at all, so SET body = EXCLUDED.body DELETES what the live row carries today — the pre-A-148 prose the surfaces print. STOP.
theThreeStatesItDistinguishes.emptyPreviews: nothing would be written, with the reason string (empty --parcel cohort: no non-absence zoning-fact atom with a non-empty district; or the warm-gate decline with its named code; or mechanical verify did not pass)

honestCaveatsDocumentedInTheRunbook: The preview's contentHash is NOT the hash the apply leg stores: emitSetbackRule / emitBuildableEnvelope stamp extractedAt/fetchedAt at emit time and contentHash derives from them. The runbook compares the STORED content_hash before/after instead. A preview hash must never be compared to a stored hash.
The dry leg reads the same live layer-23 record one execution earlier, so its detector verdict is as fresh as its own wall clock; steps 3 and 4 should run back to back.

The dry leg reports; it never refuses. Whether a payload with no conflict is acceptable is the operator's call (for 48021:34049 it is the whole point of the run), and a preview that refused to show such a payload could not tell the operator the A-148 predicate did not fire.

serialization.theFinding: writePropertyAtom takes NO LEASE. There is no mutual exclusion from the storage layer for this write; the last writer wins silently. The leases exist ONLY on the batch path (writePropertyAtomsBatch requires a HeldLease and throws LeaseRequiredError without one), which is not the path promoteDepthWarmToStorage uses.
serialization.whatTheWrapperDoesInstead: It cannot rely on the storage layer, so the exclusion is the runbook's step-2 preflight, which is documented as a HUMAN check that can be wrong: list running executions of hauska-engine-depth-warm-remint, hauska-engine-atoms-writer and hauska-engine-footprint-retag, and confirm no depth-warm cohort run with --city-cohort --force-overwrite is in flight over the parcel's jurisdiction. If it cannot be established that no other lane is re-minting the same parcel, the runbook says write that down and do not run.
whatItWouldCollideWith: the cohort arm of this same runner over an overlapping parcel set (different cohort, same atoms)
a future per-parcel run of another lane
any in-place fix-up script addressing the same rows (e.g. stamp-bastrop-successor-zoning-fact.mjs, which writes into the same atoms table)
serialization.schedulerExposure: The atoms store has NO confirmed scheduled writer. factory-conformant-reap (*/10 * * * *) and factory-publish-gate-sched-hourly (0 * * * *) run on the FACTORY store, not the atoms store. So the realistic collision is a concurrent human/agent execution, not a cron — which is worse, because an unlisted seat run is invisible to the preflight.
serialization.whyNoLockWasInvented: Adding a lease/lock to writePropertyAtom is a storage-layer change touching the atom store's write path, outside this worktree's remit and outside the ruling, and it would change the semantics of every existing writer. It is named as a leave-behind instead of being smuggled in.

rollbackArtifact.theFinding: There is NO rollback target. The write is an in-place upsert over body/fetched_at/updated_at with no version row and no history table for property atoms. Therefore the ONLY rollback artifact that can exist is a read-only capture of the live row taken before the write, and it only exists if someone takes it.
rollbackArtifact.sql_wired_as_runbook_step_1: SELECT atom_did, entity_id, content_hash, fetched_at, updated_at, body FROM atoms WHERE entity_type = 'setback-rule' AND (entity_id = '<nodeId>' OR entity_id LIKE '<nodeId>:%') AND COALESCE(body->>'status','active') = 'active';  — plus the same query for entity_type = 'buildable-envelope' and, when the parcel's geometry is in question, for the boundary-edge rows.
howTheRunbookWiresIt: Step 1 is expressly READ-ONLY and mandatory before anything else; the single-parcel arm's contract form of the query is given verbatim, and the LIKE '<nodeId>:%' arm is called out as covering the suffixed variants.
The operator saves both result sets to a dated file outside the repo and is told that losing that file IS losing the rollback.

The operator records the content_hash of each captured row. That stored hash is the before/after discriminator: step 5 re-runs the same query and requires a CHANGED content_hash when something was rewritten, or the SAME one when the re-mint was a no-op. The wrapper echoes each atom's contentHash in the dry-leg preview as well.
The runbook states plainly that a 0-row capture means there is nothing to roll back and the apply leg would INSERT a brand-new atom — a different act from a re-mint, needing its own decision.

The reversal is given as an explicit UPDATE restoring the captured body, content_hash and updated_at, together with its limitations: it restores ONE row from ONE capture, it is itself an unversioned in-place write with no lease, no gate and no dry leg, no Cloud Run Job restores a property atom, and it does not undo the boundary-edge atoms written in phase 1.
It also warns that the restored content_hash matches the captured one, so a later reader cannot tell a rollback happened — say so where the run is recorded.
rollbackArtifact.note: The wrapper does NOT automate the capture: automating a store read from the job would imply the job owns the rollback, and the rollback is deliberately an operator act on the record of the run.

The runner's full gate list for the apply leg was read, not exercised: gateWarmCohort / assertWarmGateApplied were confirmed by grep to read no environment, but whether a particular parcel passes them (i.e. whether 48021:34049 has a live, resolved, account-keyed parcel-node anchor with geometry reducible to one ring) was NOT measured for any parcel — the wrapper's own sub-tests never touch a store.

The cost of one apply execution (the single-parcel run still pages the jurisdiction's whole layer-23 feature index in the bulk acquisition step) is not measured; --task-timeout=3600 is a hang bound chosen for that reason, not a measured budget.
Whether the atoms store receives any write from an unlisted lane at the moment of a future execution cannot be established from here; the preflight is a human check.
The .mjs runner is not covered by tsc (it is plain JS): its correctness rests on `node --check` plus the vitest contract test's assertions on the runner's text, not on typechecking.
dangers: STATE IT FIRST: this wrapper is NOT yet a code gate. The depth-warm runner has no refuseApplyOutsideCloudRunJob call the way write-building-footprint-county.mjs does (writer-apply-lease.mjs exports it; P-169 wired it into that writer only). P-169 holds for this path BY CONSTRUCTION because the job runs as a Cloud Run Job, but a laptop that sets PROPERTY_ATOM_PATH=1 and runs the runner with --promote still writes. The ruling's enforcement here is procedural, not mechanical.

PARTIAL PROMOTION: promoteDepthWarmToStorage persists boundary-edge atoms FIRST, then the property atoms, then does the read-back verify. A timeout, OOM or cancellation between those phases leaves a half-promoted parcel — new boundary edges, old setback-rule — and --max-retries=0 will not repair it. The runbook's post-check covers setback-rule and buildable-envelope; the boundary-edge rows must be captured too if the parcel's geometry is in question.

SILENT SUCCESS, TWO WAYS: PROPERTY_ATOM_PATH unset (impossible through the job, possible by hand — see the stamp-bastrop-successor-zoning-fact.mjs precedent where a naive caller reports 'stamped' while writing nothing) and the conflict detectors not firing (the run exits 0, the promoted count rises, and the disclosure is unchanged). Only the dry-leg preview and the before/after content_hash diff separate these from a real re-mint.

DELETING THE PROSE CONFESSION: because the write replaces body wholesale, an emit that carries no secondSource DELETES the disclosure the live row has today. The preview flags it (deletesExistingDisclosure) but nothing BLOCKS it — the flag is advice. If the operator proceeds past a flagged preview, the pre-A-148 prose is gone and only the step-1 capture can bring it back.
NO MUTUAL EXCLUSION: two concurrent re-mints of the same parcel interleave at the body level with no lock and no error. Nothing detects it afterwards except a content_hash that changed twice.

THE PREVIEW HASH TRAP: comparing the dry leg's contentHash to the stored content_hash will ALWAYS show a difference (extractedAt/fetchedAt are stamped at emit) and could be misread as 'the write landed'. The runbook forbids it; the failure is one careless glance away.

THE A-148 SHAPE DOES NOT FIRE FOR THE FIRST USE CASE: re-minting 48021:34049 today adds the two-instrument R-1 conflict sentence (shape 'second-source'), NOT the A-148 stale-numeric-columns sentence. Anyone who re-mints this parcel expecting the One Click 25/5/25-versus-text sentence will not get it from the layer this job reads, and should not conclude the wrapper is broken.

TIMEOUT AS THE ONLY HANG BOUND: --task-timeout=3600 is the only thing bounding a hung upstream fetch in the bulk layer-23 acquisition; there is no per-request timeout imposed by this job beyond what the adapter already has.
leave_behind: The obvious next gate: call refuseApplyOutsideCloudRunJob (packages/engine-core/scripts/writer-apply-lease.mjs) from depth-warm-city-batch.mjs on the --promote arm, so P-169 stops being procedural for this runner. That is a runner change with a blast radius beyond the re-mint arm (it would affect the cohort form too) and it was deliberately NOT done here — it is the operator's/planner's call whether the cohort form should also be frozen to Cloud Run Jobs.

writePropertyAtom takes no lease while writePropertyAtomsBatch does. Unifying that (a lease, or an explicit documented exemption with a comment at the singular call site) is a storage-layer decision, NOT a re-mint fix; it was left alone because it changes the semantics of every existing writer.

No Cloud Run Job restores a property atom. If property-atom rollback matters, the rollback UPDATE in this runbook is the only mechanism and it is break-glass. A gated restore job, or a version/history table for property atoms, does not exist.

No runbook documented the per-parcel arm before this one; doc_repo/90_runbooks/factory_2_jurisdiction_depth.md documents only the city-cohort form. That doc still does not mention the per-parcel arm or the new job — pointing it at RUNBOOK.depth-warm-remint.md is a doc_repo edit outside this worktree.

stamp-bastrop-successor-zoning-fact.mjs reports status 'stamped' with atomDid undefined when PROPERTY_ATOM_PATH is unset. It writes to the same atoms table. Someone should fix that null check; it is unrelated to this wrapper and was not touched.

The runbook's apply step still requires a human to remember to run steps 1-3 first. Nothing enforces the order. A future improvement would be an --require-capture flag or a job that refuses to start without a fresh capture path, but that presupposes the operator wants the wrapper to own the rollback artifact.
limitsAcknowledged: Authored and merged only. Deploying the job is a separate operator gate, requested by the planner, not fired here.
